extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, patent attorneys/agents, parties appearing before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing appeals, contested cases, inter partes proceedings, and related petitions before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (Part 41, MPEP). Includes filing, timing, content, jurisdiction, fees, and conduct requirements for parties and counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy (Part 41 scope and construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 41 governs appeals and interferences before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Sections 1.1 to 1.36 and 1.181 to 1.183 of this title also apply to practice before the Board, as do other sections of part 1 of this title that are incorporated by reference into part 41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions of Part 41 shall be construed to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution of every proceeding before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must act with courtesy and decorum in all proceedings before the Board, including interactions with other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise clear from context, specific terms are defined for proceedings under this part (e.g., Affidavit, Board, Final, Hearing, Rehearing, Office, Panel, Panel proceeding, Party, Board member, Contested case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine who counts as a party, what constitutes a final Board action, the makeup of panels, and the meaning of contested case for application of Part 41 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must be addressed to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge. A panel or an administrative patent judge may certify a question of policy to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge for decision. The Chief Administrative Patent Judge may delegate authority to decide petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope: covers petitions on matters pending before the Board (§§ 41.35, 41.64, 41.103, and 41.205); certain matters are not subject to petition. Petition fee (see § 41.20(a)) must accompany petitions except no fee for petitions seeking supervisory review. Filing time: generally within 14 days from the date of the action from which relief is requested; requests for reconsideration of a petition decision within 14 days of the decision unless Board sets other time. A party may not file an opposition or reply to a petition without Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — extensions and late filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time will be granted only on a showing of good cause except as otherwise provided by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filings that cause abandonment or termination may be revived as set forth in § 1.137. Late filings that do not cause abandonment or termination will be excused upon a showing of excusable neglect or a Board determination that consideration on the merits would be in the interest of justice. Certain filings related to Board proceedings (e.g., extensions during prosecution, filing briefs or requests for oral hearing, seeking judicial review) are governed by other sections and not by the general extension rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel appearance, disqualification, withdrawal, and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Board has jurisdiction: the Board may authorize a person other than a registered practitioner to appear pro hac vice. The Board may disqualify counsel in a specific proceeding after notice and an opportunity to be heard. Counsel may not withdraw from a proceeding before the Board unless the Board authorizes such withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to disqualify is not final for judicial review until certified by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge. The Board may institute proceedings under this section on its own or a party may request relief. Possible violations of disciplinary rules in part 11 may be referred to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (see § 11.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of Board records and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Board action is available for public inspection without a party’s permission if rendered in a file open to the public pursuant to § 1.11 or in an application published under §§ 1.211–1.221. The Office may independently publish any Board action that is available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director believes special circumstances warrant publication of an otherwise non-publishable Board action, a party will be notified and may object in writing within two months on trade secret/confidentiality grounds and must state specific deletions needed. If entire action must be withheld, the party must explain why. The party will have not less than 20 days to request reconsideration and seek court review before contested portions are made public over objection. Record availability: generally available unless a patent application not otherwise public is involved; after final Board action, the record will be made public if involved files become open or published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of the record — expungement and refiling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may expunge any paper directed to a Board proceeding, or filed while an application or patent is under the jurisdiction of the Board, that is not authorized under this part or in a Board order, or that is filed contrary to a Board order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may not file a paper previously filed in the same Board proceeding, not even as an exhibit or appendix, without Board authorization or as required by rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices (real party-in-interest and related proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify: (1) its real party-in-interest, and (2) each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect, or be affected by, the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board of the judicial review within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal, including a copy of the complaint or notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action by owner (entire interest or part interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner of the entire interest in an application or patent involved in a Board proceeding may act in the proceeding to the exclusion of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An owner of a part interest may petition to act to the exclusion of an inventor or co-owner; the petition must show inability or refusal of an inventor or co-owner to prosecute the proceeding or other cause why it is in the interest of justice to permit action by the part owner. An order granting such petition may set conditions on actions of the parties. (Note: para. (a) revisions apply to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on or after Sept. 16, 2012; pre-AIA version is provided separately.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as the Board may otherwise direct, correspondence in an application or patent involved in an appeal during the period from appeal docketing notice issuance until decision should be mailed to: Patent Trial and Appeal Board, USPTO, PO Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313–1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailed correspondence in interfer­ence shall be sent to Mail Stop INTERFERENCE, Patent Trial and Appeal Board, PO Box 1450. Correspondence in trial proceedings (part 42) are governed by § 42.6(b). Additional address guidance appears in § 1.1(a)(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications in inter partes/contested proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte communication about an inter partes reexamination or about a contested case with a Board member, or with a Board employee assigned to the proceeding, is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For any United States Supreme Court decision, citation to the United States Reports is preferred. For any decision other than a United States Supreme Court decision, citation to the West Reporter System is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations must include pinpoint citations whenever a specific holding or portion of an authority is invoked. Non-binding authority should be used sparingly; if the authority is not an Office authority and is not reproduced in the United States Reports or the West Reporter System, a copy of the authority should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees (petition and appeal fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for filing petitions to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge under § 41.3 is $452.00. Fees for filing a notice of appeal and other appeal-related fees vary by entity status (micro, small, other than small or micro) and filing type (notice of appeal, brief in inter partes reexamination, request for oral hearing, forwarding an appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide amounts for micro entity, small entity, and other than small/micro for: notice of appeal, filing briefs in inter partes reexamination, requests for oral hearing, and forwarding appeals to the Board. See § 41.20(b) and the referenced tables for exact amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart B definitions (Applicant, Evidence, Owner, Proceeding, Record)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to § 41.2, the following definitions apply to ex parte appeals: Applicant means the applicant in a national application or reissue; Evidence means something that tends to prove or disprove a fact (excluding dictionaries for this subpart); Owner means the owner of the patent undergoing ex parte reexamination; Proceeding and Record are defined for appeal context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record includes Image File Wrapper items of the official file excluding unentered amendments, Evidence and other documents not entered; for issued patents being reissued or reexamined, Record includes the Record of the patent being reissued or reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to take an appeal (notice of appeal; who may appeal; timing and presumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is taken to the Board by filing a notice of appeal. Every applicant whose claim has been twice rejected may appeal by filing a notice of appeal accompanied by the fee within the time provided under § 1.134 for reply. Similar provisions for owners in ex parte reexamination are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature requirements of §§ 1.33 and 11.18(a) do not apply to a notice of appeal. An appeal is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless cancelled by an amendment entered by the Office. Time periods for filing may be extendable under § 1.136 for patent applications and § 1.550(c) for ex parte reexams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits/evidence after appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after filing an appeal and prior to the date a brief is filed may be admitted as provided in § 1.116. Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted: (1) to cancel claims where cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim, or (2) to rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by §§ 41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), and 41.50(b)(1). An affidavit or other Evidence filed after filing an appeal and prior to the date of filing a brief may be admitted if the examiner determines it overcomes all rejections under appeal and that good and sufficient reasons why it was necessary and not earlier presented have been made. Other affidavits/evidence filed after appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by listed sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction over appeal (beginning, end, remand, effect of filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon the filing of a reply brief under § 41.41 or the expiration of the time in which to file such a reply brief, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction ends when: Director or Board enters a remand order; Board enters a final decision and judicial review is sought or time expires; an express abandonment complying with § 1.138 is recognized; an RCE is filed complying with § 1.114; appellant fails to take required action under specified sections and Board enters dismissal; appellant reopens prosecution pursuant to § 41.40(b) or in response to a new ground entered in a Board decision. Director may sua sponte order remand prior to decision. Documents filed during Board jurisdiction (except authorized petitions) are held in abeyance until Board jurisdiction ends. The Board may administratively relinquish jurisdiction to the examiner if the file is incomplete or noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief timing and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal. The appeal brief fee in an application or ex parte reexamination is $0.00, but if the appeal results in an examiner’s answer, the appeal forwarding fee must be paid within the time specified in § 41.45 to avoid dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the brief within the specified period results in dismissal of the appeal. Time periods are extendable under § 1.136 for patent applications and § 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief content and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, the brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals, interferences, and trials; (iii) Summary of claimed subject matter; (iv) Argument with respect to each ground of rejection and the basis therefor; (v) Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: (i) identify real party in interest by name unless inventors are themselves the real party in interest; (ii) identify related cases by application/patent/appeal/interference/trial number that involve an application or patent owned by the appellant or assignee and may affect the Board decision; (iii) provide concise explanation of subject matter defined in each rejected independent claim with references to the specification in the Record (page/line or paragraph) and drawings by reference characters; if a claim contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), identify corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification by reference; reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy this requirement; (iv) arguments must explain why the examiner erred, with citations of statutes/regulations/authorities/Record; any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52; each ground contested must be argued under a separate heading that reasonably identifies the ground; for grounds applying to multiple claims, claims may be argued separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes waiver of argument for separate patentability; a statement merely pointing out what a claim recites is not an argument for separate patentability; (v) include an appendix containing a copy of the claims involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including new amendments or evidence in appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 for treatment of amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after final action but before or on the same date of filing an appeal and § 41.33 for treatment of amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing the appeal. Review of examiner’s refusal to admit an amendment or Evidence is by petition to the Director (§ 1.181).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of non-compliance for appeal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with all requirements, appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a time period to file an amended brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not timely file an amended brief that overcomes all reasons for non-compliance, the appeal will stand dismissed. Review of non-compliance determinations is by petition to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge (§ 41.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer content and new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief. An examiner’s answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken unless the examiner’s answer expressly indicates a ground has been withdrawn. An examiner’s answer may include a new ground of rejection, which must be designated as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection relying on Evidence not relied upon in the Office action shall be designated as a new ground. The examiner must obtain Director approval to furnish an answer that includes a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s options in response to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer exercise one of two options to avoid sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the new ground: (1) Reopen prosecution, or (2) Maintain appeal by filing a reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopen prosecution: request reopening before primary examiner by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits (§§ 1.130–1.132) or other Evidence relevant to the new ground; such a request will be entered and treated as request to withdraw the appeal. Maintain appeal: file a reply brief as set forth in § 41.41 addressing each new ground and following other brief requirements; a reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit or other Evidence — if accompanied it will be treated as request to reopen prosecution. Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) do not apply to the time period set in this section; see § 1.136(b) and § 1.550(c) for extensions to reply.
